metadata.description: AAV serotype tropism reference for gene therapy target validation
metadata.methodology: Double-blind LLM query - spawned subagent with NO context about therapies, diseases, or validation goals. The subagent answered tropism questions based on training knowledge without knowing why we were asking.

methodology_details.approach: Double-blind query using isolated LLM subagent
methodology_details.prompt_template: What are the primary cell types transduced by [serotype] after [route] delivery? Rank by transduction efficiency. Do NOT mention any specific therapies or diseases.
methodology_details.why_this_works: The analyst (subagent) cannot cherry-pick evidence to support an unknown hypothesis
previous_failures: Web searches were contaminated by therapy literature
LLM queries with analyst context led to cherry-picking
methodology_details.key_insight: Both the query AND the analyst must be blind to eliminate confirmation bias

AAV9.description: Most widely used for CNS gene therapy; crosses blood-brain barrier after IV delivery. First AAV serotype shown to achieve significant brain transduction after IV administration.

age_dependence.description: Transduction pattern varies dramatically by age at injection
age_dependence.neonatal: Primarily neuronal transduction throughout brain and spinal cord, including motor neurons (84-99% motor neuron transduction in spinal cord)
age_dependence.adult: Preferentially targets astrocytes; neuronal transduction significantly reduced

source.citation: Foust KD et al. Nat Biotechnol. 2009;27(1):59-65
source.quote: Intravenous injection of AAV9 in neonatal mice results in primarily neuronal transduction throughout the brain and spinal cord, but preferentially targets astrocytes when injected in mice greater than 2 weeks of age

species_dependence.mice: Efficient neuronal transduction after IV administration
species_dependence.nhp_human: Primarily glial transduction (astrocytes, microglia); neuronal transduction much lower

source.quote: Unlike in mice where AAV9 efficiently transduces neurons following IV administration, in non-human primates (NHPs) and humans this route results primarily in glial transduction, with astrocytes and microglia being the most prominently targeted cell types

liver_off_target.description: Substantial hepatic transduction accompanies CNS targeting
liver_off_target.magnitude: 300-1000 fold higher transduction in liver compared to CNS
liver_off_target.mitigation: Tissue-specific promoters can limit off-target expression

liver.notes: DOMINANT SINK after IV delivery. Receives 100-1000x more vector genomes than other tissues. This is the PRIMARY target regardless of therapeutic intent.

blind_validation.source: Blind LLM query with no therapy context
blind_validation.quote: Liver is the dominant 'sink' for AAV9 after IV delivery; receives 100-1000x more vector genomes than other tissues

cardiac.notes: AAV9 has excellent cardiac tropism; heart is among the most efficiently transduced organs after liver.

blind_validation.source: Blind LLM query with no therapy context

skeletal_muscle.notes: Strong transduction throughout skeletal muscle including diaphragm.

cns.notes: AAV9 crosses BBB and transduces CNS neurons BROADLY - not motor-neuron-specific. Motor neurons are transduced because they are neurons, not because AAV9 has special motor neuron tropism. Age-dependent: neonatal=neuronal, adult=glial.
cns.bias_correction: Previous claim of 'motor neuron tropism' was derived from SMA therapy literature, not general tropism studies. AAV9 has no preferential motor neuron targeting.

blind_validation.source: Blind LLM query with no therapy context
blind_validation.quote: CNS neurons (broadly) - AAV9 crosses the blood-brain barrier, transducing cortical neurons, Purkinje cells, spinal motor neurons

pns.notes: DRG neurons efficiently transduced. This is BOTH therapeutically useful AND a safety concern (DRG toxicity observed in trials).
pns.safety_note: DRG exposure implicated in AAV gene therapy safety findings

blind_validation.source: Blind LLM query with no therapy context
blind_validation.quote: Dorsal root ganglia (DRG) neurons - Efficiently transduced; this is actually a safety concern (DRG toxicity)

IV.notes: Standard route for Zolgensma (neonatal/infant administration). Age at injection critically affects neuronal vs glial tropism.

intrathecal.notes: Direct CNS delivery; lower peripheral exposure. May achieve better neuronal transduction in adults than IV.

intracerebroventricular.notes: Targets ventricular system; limited parenchymal penetration

AAV2.description: First AAV used clinically; limited spread, good for local delivery. Neuronal preference after direct brain injection.

cns_intracranial.notes: Strong neuronal tropism at injection site; limited spread due to heparan sulfate binding

blind_validation.source: Blind LLM query with no therapy context
blind_validation.quote: AAV2 has strong neuronal tropism; efficiently transduces neurons at injection site. Astrocytes transduced but less efficiently than neurons. Oligodendrocytes low, Microglia very poor/minimal.

retina_subretinal.notes: Gold standard for subretinal delivery; RPE is primary target, photoreceptors well transduced

blind_validation.source: Blind LLM query with no therapy context
blind_validation.quote: RPE - primary target, very efficiently transduced. Photoreceptors (rods and cones) - well transduced from the subretinal space. Muller glia - lower efficiency transduction.

intracranial.notes: Used for Upstaza/Kebilidi; stereotactic injection to putamen. Limited spread from injection site.

blind_validation.source: Blind LLM query with no therapy context
blind_validation.quote: AAV2 has poor diffusion through brain parenchyma; transduction is largely confined to the injection site. Heparan sulfate binding limits spread but concentrates transduction locally.

subretinal.notes: Used for Luxturna; excellent RPE transduction, moderate photoreceptor transduction

blind_validation.source: Blind LLM query with no therapy context
blind_validation.quote: Subretinal injection places vector directly adjacent to RPE and photoreceptors. Intravitreal AAV2 would primarily transduce inner retinal layers (ganglion cells).

intravitreal.notes: Limited penetration to outer retina; ganglion cell layer is primary target

AAV5.description: Liver-tropic but with lower efficiency than AAV8. Key advantage is low seroprevalence (less pre-existing immunity).

lower_efficiency.description: AAV5 has lower hepatocyte transduction efficiency than AAV8

source.quote: AAV5 can only facilitate a low level of transgene expression in the liver, constraining its application to a small number of liver diseases

seroprevalence_advantage.description: Lower pre-existing immunity in human population
seroprevalence_advantage.clinical_relevance: Chosen for Hemgenix despite lower efficiency due to immunological advantages

liver.notes: Moderate liver tropism - lower efficiency than AAV8 but advantageous seroprevalence profile.

blind_validation.source: Blind LLM query with no therapy context
blind_validation.quote: AAV5 has moderate liver tropism. Lower overall efficiency - AAV5 is generally less efficient than AAV8 or AAV9 for liver transduction.

lung.notes: Originally isolated from human samples; has airway tropism. Uses N-linked sialic acid as receptor.

cns_neurons.age_considerations: AAV9 IV preferentially transduces neurons in neonates but astrocytes in adults
cns_neurons.species_considerations: AAV9 IV transduces neurons better in mice than in NHPs/humans

cns_glia.notes: AAV9 IV in adults preferentially targets astrocytes. Microglia are difficult to transduce with any AAV.

retinal.notes: Subretinal delivery targets RPE and photoreceptors; intravitreal targets ganglion cells

muscle.notes: AAVrh74 is most muscle-specific; AAV9 also transduces muscle but with CNS off-target

liver.notes: AAV8 has highest hepatocyte efficiency (90-95%). AAV5 lower but better seroprevalence. AAV9 liver is off-target.

hematopoietic.description: Blood and immune cells (not AAV targets - use lentivirus/retrovirus ex vivo)
hematopoietic.notes: HSCs are difficult to transduce with AAV; ex vivo lentiviral transduction used instead

methodology.approach: Double-blind LLM query - spawned a subagent with NO context about this project, therapies, diseases, or what we were trying to validate
methodology.prompt_used: Answer these questions about adeno-associated virus (AAV) tropism... What are the primary cell types transduced by [serotype] after [route] delivery? Rank them by transduction efficiency. Do NOT mention any specific therapies or diseases.
methodology.why_this_works: The analyst (subagent) doesn't know WHY we're asking, so cannot cherry-pick evidence to support an unknown hypothesis

previous_failure.problem: Web searches and previous LLM queries were contaminated because the analyst (me) had full context about Zolgensma, SMA, and motor neurons
previous_failure.result: Cherry-picked quotes mentioning motor neurons because that's what I was primed to look for
previous_failure.lesson: Blind queries aren't enough - the analyst must ALSO be blind

primary_tropisms_ranked: 1. Hepatocytes (DOMINANT SINK - 100-1000x more vector genomes than other tissues)

key_corrections.liver_ranking: Liver should be ranked FIRST, not fourth. Previous data underestimated liver as 'off-target' when it's actually the dominant target.
key_corrections.motor_neurons: Motor neurons are NOT a primary AAV9 tropism - they are simply neurons in the CNS that get transduced. The emphasis on 'motor neurons' came FROM SMA therapy context.
key_corrections.skeletal_muscle: Skeletal muscle was underranked; blind query places it third.

caveats_confirmed.age_dependence: BBB crossing much more efficient in neonates than adults
caveats_confirmed.species_differences: Mouse CNS transduction is higher than in NHPs or humans
caveats_confirmed.liver_sequestration: Liver captures most of the vector, limiting delivery to other organs

bias_detected.status: BIASED - this claim originated from therapy-specific literature, not general tropism studies
bias_detected.correct_statement: AAV9 broadly transduces CNS neurons (including motor neurons) after crossing BBB. Motor neurons are not preferentially targeted vs other CNS neurons.
bias_detected.implication_for_validation: The 'aav_reachable' match for Zolgensma is STILL VALID because AAV9 does transduce CNS neurons including motor neurons - the bias was in claiming motor neurons as a PRIMARY tropism

other_serotypes_validated.AAV2_intracranial: CONFIRMED - neurons at injection site, limited spread, poor glial transduction
other_serotypes_validated.AAV5_IV: CONFIRMED - hepatocytes, lower efficiency than AAV8
other_serotypes_validated.AAVrh74_IV: CONFIRMED - skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle, lower liver than AAV8/9
